4.en: ‘We are neither spies, soldiers, nor enforcers, yet we are all these at once. We are whatever the Imperium needs us to be. We alone know the horrors that await Mankind should the Imperium fall, so we alone are willing to do whatever it takes to prevent it. Whatever that makes us.’

22.en: In legend, an Inquisitor’s authority is second only to the Emperor Himself. Their holy duty is to identify and resolve threats within the Imperium: psykers, mutants, rebellion, corruption, xenos entities, and even traitorous incompetence fall under their jurisdiction. None are beyond their reach or above their scrutiny; even the most resolute, including the High Lords of Terra, are all vulnerable to corruption and failure. Ambition and greed cause immeasurable damage alone, but worse, they provide fertile soil for the Ruinous Powers to fester.

26.en: Inquisitors are terrifying individuals; in many cases, they are just as unnerving as the inhuman enemies they hunt. The burden of power they must wield is staggering. If their task suits them, Inquisitors can call on the resources of an entire world. Space Marine Chapters, @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.r6JYS3jOfrAEorvd]{Astra Militarum}, Adepta Sororitas, and even Imperial Assassins are at their beck and call.

30.en: But Inquisitors know they must tread carefully with their authority; as much as they know their enemies, they understand the duplicitous nature of the Imperium’s factions and political landscape. Resources are finite, influence is never a guarantee, and bureaucracy always delays. Most Inquisitors prefer to operate from the shadows, employing acolytes and deniable assets to operate with utmost discretion.

50.en: Most have already proven themselves against the foes of the Emperor in one way or another — as battlehardened warriors, battlefleet generals, or indomitable psykers. Others may rise through an Inquisitor’s retinue via a direct apprenticeship as their Interrogator, an Inquisitor’s most trusted and capable acolyte, inheriting the position and power upon their mentor’s demise or when their master considers them ready for elevation.

54.en: It is a terrible truth that most Inquisitors die in service to the Emperor, survive long enough to succumb to radicalised ideas, or become corrupted by the Ruinous Powers they fight — an unfortunate byproduct of their necessary individualised methods and selfgarnered philosophies. Indeed, a staggering number of Inquisitors rose to their position by eliminating their former mentors as prime judges or witnesses of their fall from purity.

58.en: The threats they face are so beyond reason that the fear and antipathy they spread is a necessary evil of their work, all in service to the Imperium. Inquisitors know their duty must be unwavering, and mercy is a luxury no one can afford. No threat, within, without, or beyond, would hold back from eradicating Humankind if it gained a single foothold. They know that if one planet falls, certainly the next will, and so on, until hundreds of worlds and billions of lives are lost.

74.en: Each Inquisitor, upon their ascension, forges a badge of office that admits them the highest level of clearance across the Imperium. This artefact is called an @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-items.Item.UmYkx98dKv97QSJy]{Inquisitorial Rosette}, and many of them have ingrained the Inquisitor’s genetic encoding within them. The Inquisitor designs their Rosette to represent their aesthetics, history, and mission, becoming a unique identifier of their authority. Theoretically, a Rosette can bypass any lock or barrier, physical or bureaucratic, that gets in the way of their investigation — the only barrier it cannot bypass is fickle Human behaviour.
